---
title: "Loads and grids"
---

The surface loads, time histories and ocean basins of the two benchmarks, and
the grid GIAMIP prescribes. Generated from `gia_mip/resources/loads/` and `gia_mip/grids.py`.

## Spada et al. (2011): three analytic loads

Each is axisymmetric about its own centre, given as a surface mass density
against colatitude with a closed form for its Legendre coefficients. Mass is
not conserved: there is no ocean in this benchmark, so nothing compensates the
load.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("../..").resolve()))
from IPython.display import Markdown
from gia_mip import cases
t = cases.loads("spada2011")
out = []
for key, L in t["loads"].items():
    out.append(f"### {L['name']}\n")
    out.append("```\n" + L["surface_mass_density"] + "\n```\n")
    out.append("Legendre coefficients:\n\n```\n" + L["legendre_coefficients"] + "\n```\n")
    numbers = [f"{k.replace('_', ' ')}: {v}" for k, v in L.items()
               if k not in ("name", "surface_mass_density",
                            "legendre_coefficients", "note")]
    if numbers:
        out.append("Reference values: " + ", ".join(numbers) + ".\n")
    if L.get("note"):
        out.append(L["note"] + "\n")
Markdown("\n".join(out))
```

### Constants

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("../..").resolve()))
from IPython.display import Markdown
from gia_mip import cases
c = cases.loads("spada2011")["constants"]
rows = ["| Constant | Value |", "| --- | ---: |"]
for k, v in c.items():
    if k.startswith("$"):
        continue
    rows.append(f"| {k.replace('_', ' ')} | {v} |")
rows.append("")
rows.append("::: {.callout-important}")
rows.append(c["$comment"])
rows.append(":::")
Markdown("\n".join(rows))
```

## Martinec et al. (2018): ice, time and basins

Every case uses the same cap shape, with an angular radius of 10 degrees,
moved and rescaled.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("../..").resolve()))
from IPython.display import Markdown
from gia_mip import cases
t = cases.loads("martinec2018")
out = ["### Ice height models\n",
       "| Model | Centre colatitude | Centre longitude | Height (m) | Note |",
       "| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |"]
for k, v in t["ice_height_models"].items():
    out.append(f"| {k} | {v['centre_colatitude_deg']} | {v['centre_longitude_deg']} | "
               f"{v['height_m']} | {v.get('note', '')} |")

out.append("\n### Time scenarios\n")
for k, v in t["time_scenarios"].items():
    out.append(f"**{k}** {v['description']} Terminal time {v['terminal_time_kyr']} kyr.\n")

out.append("\n### Ocean basins\n")
out.append("```\n" + t["ocean_basins"]["$formula"] + "\n```\n")
out.append(f"with sigma_b = {t['ocean_basins']['sigma_b_deg']} degrees.\n")
out.append("| Basin | Centre colatitude | Centre longitude | bmax (m) | b0 (m) | Max depth (m) | Note |")
out.append("| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |")
for k, v in t["ocean_basins"].items():
    if k.startswith("$") or k == "sigma_b_deg":
        continue
    out.append(f"| {k} | {v['centre_colatitude_deg']} | {v['centre_longitude_deg']} | "
               f"{v['bmax_m']} | {v['b0_m']} | {v.get('max_depth_m', '-')} | {v.get('note', '')} |")

out.append("\n### Sea level equation levels\n")
for k, v in t["sea_level_equation_levels"].items():
    out.append(f"- **{k}** {v}")
out.append("")
for n in t.get("notes", []):
    out.append(f"- {n}")
Markdown("\n".join(out))
```

## The GIAMIP grid

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("../..").resolve()))
from IPython.display import Markdown
import numpy as np
from gia_mip import grids

lat, lon = grids.latitudes(), grids.longitudes()
spacing = np.diff(lat)
areas = grids.cell_areas(6371000.0)
ratio = areas.sum() / (4 * np.pi * 6371000.0 ** 2)

table = f"""
A Gauss-Legendre quadrature grid, {grids.NLAT} latitudes by {grids.NLON}
longitudes, integrating exactly to spherical harmonic degree {grids.LMAX}.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Latitudes | {grids.NLAT}, the Gauss-Legendre nodes in sin(latitude) |
| First and last latitude | {lat[0]:.5f}, {lat[-1]:.5f} degrees |
| Latitude spacing | {spacing.min():.4f} at the pole to {spacing.max():.4f} degrees at the equator |
| Longitudes | {grids.NLON}, equally spaced over [0, 360) |
| Longitude step | {lon[1] - lon[0]:.6f} degrees |
| Last longitude | {lon[-1]:.5f} degrees, so 360 is not a repeat of 0 |
| Cell area | the quadrature weight times the longitude step times the radius squared |
| Total area check | {ratio:.15f} of 4 pi a squared |
"""
Markdown(table)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Two ways to get this grid wrong

The latitudes are not equally spaced, and neither pole is a grid point. The
area of a cell is the quadrature weight times the longitude step, because on
a sphere the area element is `a^2 dlambda d(sin phi)` and the weights
integrate `d(sin phi)` exactly. Using `cos(lat) * dlat * dlon` gives an answer
that is wrong and looks plausible, and six of the ten variables GIAMIP
requires are area or mass integrals.

An axis built with `numpy.linspace` has the right count and the right extent
and is a different grid. `gia_mip.grids.check` rejects it.
:::
